sections.content: How many people stayed in Royal Tunbridge Wells after gaining qualifications?

Royal Tunbridge Wells is a medium-sized town in the South East. Royal Tunbridge Wells does not have its own university.

Royal Tunbridge Wells has lower levels of deprivation.

Overall, Royal Tunbridge Wells ended up with:

  • fewer graduates than it produced
  • more non-graduates with advanced qualifications than it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 2,105 state-school pupils from Royal Tunbridge Wells who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 1,010 (48%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 495 (24%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Royal Tunbridge Wells to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Royal Tunbridge Wells' pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Royal Tunbridge Wells in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Where did those who left Royal Tunbridge Wells move to?

Of Royal Tunbridge Wells's graduates, 460 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 85 of those graduates (18%) were living fairly locally, in the Tunbridge Wells travel to work area (TTWA).

Of Royal Tunbridge Wells's qualified (level 3+) non-graduates, 180 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 80 of those qualified non-graduates (44%) were living fairly locally, in the Tunbridge Wells travel to work area (TTWA).

Of those in Royal Tunbridge Wells' GCSE cohort:

  • 305 graduates left the South East
  • the most common region they moved to was London
  • 60 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates left the South East
  • the most common region they moved to was London

In 2018 to 2019, 39% of graduates and 44% of qualified non-graduates living in Royal Tunbridge Wells had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 880 graduates and 550 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in Royal Tunbridge Wells. This is compared with the 1,010 graduates and 495 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In 2018 to 2019, 60% of the graduates had also lived in Royal Tunbridge Wells as GCSE pupils, while 39% had moved there from elsewhere.

Of the qualified non-graduates who lived in Royal Tunbridge Wells in 2018 to 2019, 55% had lived there as GCSE pupils, while 44% had moved to the area from elsewhere.
